name: toolsmith-files-write
intent: Create several new files from one stdin bundle, never overwriting by accident.
use_when: You create two or more new files in one step, such as a class with its test and its docs.
You would otherwise chain several `cat > path <<'EOF'` heredocs with `mkdir -p`.
not_for: Changing an existing file: use the Edit tool or toolsmith-text-replace.
One new file: the Write tool is enough.
input: A bundle on stdin. Each file starts with a marker line, '=== <path>' (the marker, a space, the path relative to the current directory). The file's content is every following line up to the next marker line, exactly as written, blank lines included; it ends with a newline unless it is empty. Change the marker with --marker when a file has lines that start with '=== '.

options.text: Replace files that already exist (keeping their permissions) instead of refusing.
Use this text instead of '===' to start each file.

output: Before writing, every path is checked: if any already exists (without --force) or is a directory, nothing is written and stderr lists them all. Then each file is written through a temporary file and a rename, with missing parent directories created, and stdout shows 'created <path> (N lines)' or 'replaced <path> (N lines)' per file and 'Done: N files written.'

exit_codes.text: Nothing written: a path already exists or is a directory.
Nothing written: the bundle or the arguments are wrong.
A write failed after other files were written; the message lists the files already written.

examples.title: A component and its test
examples.stdin:
=== app/components/empty_state_component.rb
class EmptyStateComponent < ViewComponent::Base
end
=== test/components/empty_state_component_test.rb
require "test_helper"

class EmptyStateComponentTest < ViewComponent::TestCase
end
examples.stdout:
created app/components/empty_state_component.rb (2 lines)
created test/components/empty_state_component_test.rb (4 lines)
Done: 2 files written.

examples.title: An existing file stops the whole bundle
examples.stdin:
=== NOTES.md
- First note.
=== README.md
# New shop
examples.stderr:
toolsmith-files-write: nothing written:
  README.md already exists
Use the Edit tool or toolsmith-text-replace to change an existing file, or --force to replace it.
